name: file.write_at
description: Random-access write of `content` at byte `offset`. The chunked-upload primitive — bridges call this in sequence for files over their single-shot threshold. The file must exist (use `file.write` or `file.create` first); returns ERR not_found if absent.

path.description: Absolute path. Parent directory must exist.

offset.description: Byte offset to start writing at. The file must already exist (returns ERR not_found otherwise).

content.description: Bytes to write at `offset`. base64-encoded if encoding=binary; decoded text otherwise.

encoding.description: Encoding used to interpret `content`. Same vocabulary as file.read / file.write.

truncate.description: Only meaningful at `offset: 0` (enforced — see x-conditional). When true, clears any existing file content before writing (the canonical first-chunk-of-chunked-upload pattern).

x-conditional.description: truncate: true requires offset: 0 — truncating at a non-zero offset is undefined.

bytes_written.description: Number of bytes written at `offset` (after encoding).

new_size.description: Total file size after this write. Useful for chunked-upload progress tracking — caller knows where to set `offset` for the next chunk.

x-implementations.name: create_file_w_random_access
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateFileW` (OPEN_ALWAYS at offset=0, OPEN_EXISTING otherwise) + `SetFilePointerEx(offset)` + `WriteFile`. `truncate: true` adds `SetEndOfFile(0)` before the write.

x-implementations.name: create_file_a_random_access
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateFileA` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where CreateFileW is unavailable. Same SetFilePointerEx + WriteFile path.

windows-modern.description: CreateFileW + SetFilePointerEx + WriteFile. NOT atomic across calls (chunked writes are inherently sequential). For atomic single-shot writes, use file.write instead. Long paths via `\\?\` prefix automatic when input exceeds MAX_PATH.

windows-classic.description: CreateFileA on NT 4 / 9x; CreateFileW on NT 5+. SetFilePointerEx is NT 5+; NT 4 / 9x agents use SetFilePointer (32-bit offset) — files >4GB on classic return ERR invalid_args for offsets exceeding 32-bit range.
